en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Sixteenth Chapter
The Discourse on Matter as Ripening:
Is matter ripening? Yes.
Is form to be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful, or to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant;

is it associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, or associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; is it associated with contact … [and so on] … associated with consciousness;
is it with an object; and is there for it turning away … [and so on] … aspiration?
It should not be stated thus...
[as before] ...Is it not the case that it is neither to be experienced as pleasure nor to be experienced as pain...
[as before] ...that it is without an object, and that there is no turning toward it... [as before] ...nor aspiration for it?
“Yes.

“If it is neither to be experienced as pleasure nor to be experienced as pain … [and so on] … if it is without an object, then there is for it no turning toward … [and so on] … no aspiration. Indeed, you should not say:”
“Form is a result of kamma.
Is contact a result of kamma? Is contact to be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful … [and so on] … accompanied by an object?
Is there its turning toward [the object], … [and so on] … its aspiration?
“Yes.
“Is matter a result; is matter to be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful … [and so on] … is it with an object;
does it have turning away … [and so on] … and aspiration?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Matter is a result;
matter is neither to be experienced as pleasant nor to be experienced as painful … it is without an object,
there is no turning toward it … [as before] … nor is there any aspiration for it?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is contact a result? Is contact neither to be experienced as pleasant nor to be experienced as painful?
… [and so on] … is it without an object? Is there no turning toward it? … [and so on] … is there no aspiration for it?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “form is a result”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that the mental states and mental factors which have arisen due to the performance of karma are called ‘result’ (vipāka)?
“Yes.”
If mental states and mental factors that have arisen from the performance of karma are a result (vipāka), then indeed, O friend, you must say:
"Material form that has arisen from the performance of karma is a result.
The discussion on whether material form is a result is concluded.
